# Learn

Backgammon Made Simple uses a structured curriculum. Start with the decisions that confuse real players, then add foundations exactly when they help. The doubling cube is the first featured learning path, but it is not the whole identity of the site [@bms-fixture-curriculum].

## Curriculum

| Track | Status | What it covers |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Start Here | Available | Shared language, orientation, and the main game plans |
| Checker Play | Current | Contact positions, priorities, and tactical tradeoffs |
| Opening Play | Available | Early-roll choices and position-building |
| The Doubling Cube | Current | Money-game cube decisions and take points |
| Match Play | Coming later | Score-dependent cube and checker choices |
| Endgames | Coming later | Racing and bear-off technique |
| Engines and Analysis | Available | How to read evaluations, rollouts, and uncertainty |

> Start with the learning track that matches the decisions you want to understand now.

## Learning Path

1.  Start Here.
2.  Checker Play.
3.  Opening Play.
4.  The Doubling Cube.
5.  Match Play.
6.  Endgames.
7.  Engines and Analysis.

## Course Notes

The first lessons use short positions, simple language, and a fixed vocabulary. The later lessons add score state, volatility, and engine evidence.[^1]

### Learning Model

Term

:   A word the reader should recognize.

Take point

:   The threshold where taking starts to make sense in a money-game context.

### A Small Equation

$$EV = P_{win} \times W - P_{lose} \times L$$
